subject: Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria for CloudGoods POC
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cloudgoods.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-30T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria for CloudGoods POC

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the technical POC so we stay aligned with your internal stakeholders. I pulled together a compact evaluation playbook (links and attachments below) focused on the "model-fit" signals you called out: intent accuracy on catalog tasks, hallucination rate on pricing/contract answers, and latency under 95th%-ile SLAs.

Summary of recommended model candidates to trial (priority order):
- Mistral-7B (q4) — strong instruction-following, low latency profile for 8k windows
- Llama-2-13B (q4_0) — competitive on factual accuracy with low hallucination when paired with the prompt bundle
- OpenLlama-7B-instruct — fast and cheap baseline for throughput tests
- Redwood-Prod-Baseline (prod-staging) — our proprietary baseline (what we expect your production to look like if you take Dedicated)

Acceptance thresholds (draft):
- Core intent accuracy >= 92% on your catalog intent set (we'll use the promptset you shared).
- Hallucination incidents <= 2% (measured on the contract/pricing evaluation slice).
- 95th percentile latency <= 380ms (for single-turn catalog queries) on Redwood Dedicated profile.
- Embed similarity recall for retrieval tasks >= 0.88 (embedding vectors benchmark).

Artifacts attached / links: prompt set (cloudgoods_promptset_v1.jsonl), baseline benchmark CSV (benchmark_summary_q1.csv), and an acceptance matrix (poe_acceptance_matrix.xlsx). Also added a Drive folder with full eval harness and example runs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC-CloudGoods-benchmarks

Proposed next steps:
1) You share the final prompt/intent mapping file (if there are changes) — we have your seed set but need the full 2k examples.
2) We run 3-day automated run across the 4 model candidates and return a short readout + per-prompt failure cases.
3) Joint review with your ML/Product team and procurement (if baseline parity looks good we move to pricing/contract).

Can you confirm the evaluation window you'd prefer (we suggested Feb 7-9 to align with your product sprint) and whether Procurement should be looped in now?

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cloudgoods.com>

Date: 2027-02-01T09:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria for CloudGoods POC

Vivek — thanks for the detailed plan and the artifacts, this is helpful. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency: our security team requires that tokenized customer identifiers never leave our VPC during the POC. Is it possible to run the eval with Redwood Private in our staging VPC, or will Hosted infra be used for these runs?

2) Proprietary baseline: the internal team expects our current in-house model (AcmeNova v1) to be the primary comparator. Can you include it in the matrix or do you need us to share logs/outputs for it? We may be able to provide a sanitized export.

3) Procurement: looping them in now makes sense — they will want the expected usage profile if we move to Dedicated. Procurement (cc) — main questions will be committed QPS and overage behavior.

We can target Feb 8-10 for the runs; prefer 8th as a buffer.

—Alicia
Alicia Barnes
Head of Product, CloudGoods
A: alicia@cloudgoods.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cloudgoods.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T11:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria for CloudGoods POC

Hi Alicia — quick answers from the evaluation engineering side: 

- Residency: we can run the POC inside Redwood Private in your VPC for the metric collection portion. For model variants hosted outside the VPC (e.g., open model runners), we can bring the inputs and run locally in a controlled runner; outputs and logs can stay in your VPC. I'll coordinate with Security to create an audit plan.

- Including AcmeNova v1: yes, we can include your in-house model as a comparator. Best is a sanitized export (pairwise prompts + model outputs). If you can't share raw outputs, we can run a black-box comparative test where we send identical prompts to both Redwood candidates and AcmeNova and compare outputs. Either works.

- Quick test plan for parity checks (high level):
  * Single-turn intent eval (2k examples) — measure top-1 accuracy and confusion matrix
  * Hallucination slice (200 contract-related prompts) — manual adjudication + heuristics
  * Latency sweep (1k queries at target concurrency) — p95 measurement across runs
  * Small regeneration stress test (simulated 30% multi-turn flows) — to see KV cache benefit

We will prepare the eval harness and a rubric for adjudication on the hallucination slice. If these acceptance thresholds are acceptable to you (Vivek's numbers above), we'll lock Feb 8 start.

Jasmine
Principal Eval Engineer — Redwood Inference

(Attached: quick_rubric.md (md, 6KB))

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Barnes <alicia@cloudgoods.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, CloudGoods Procurement <procurement@cloudgoods.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & acceptance criteria for CloudGoods POC

Thanks Alicia — great, appreciate the procurement heads-up and the willingness to include AcmeNova. Finalizing scope below and proposed owners so we can issue a short mutual action plan (MAP):

Scope:
- Inputs: cloudgoods_promptset_v1.jsonl (2,000 intents + 200 contract QA prompts) — CloudGoods to confirm by Feb 4 EOD.
- Runs: Feb 8 start — 72-hour run (Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B, OpenLlama-7B, Redwood-Prod-Baseline + AcmeNova black-box).
- Outputs: per-prompt output files, adjudication notes for hallucination slice, latency p95 report, and an acceptance matrix filled by both teams.

Owners:
- CloudGoods: provide finalized prompt set and sanitized AcmeNova export (or confirm black-box test) — Alicia / Ethan
- Redwood: run benchmarks and provide initial readout + failure cases by Feb 11 — Jasmine (lead), Soojin (infra), Vivek (customer sync)
- Procurement: (cc) Redwood will share expected commit profiles after we confirm parity/run results; if parity looks good we will prepare a Dedicated proposal.

Action items (short):
1) Alicia confirm prompt set/version and whether AcmeNova export will be shared (by Feb 4).
2) Jasmine to provision runners and confirm Private VPC configuration with CloudGoods security (by Feb 5).
3) Schedule 30-min readout on Feb 11 10:00am PT — I will send calendar invite once Alicia confirms.

If that all looks right I'll send a brief MAP and calendar invite.

Best — Vivek
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
